learningObjectives: Understand basic probability concepts used in data analysis.
Differentiate population parameters from sample statistics.
Identify how sampling supports statistical inference.

activities.title: Explore Probability
activities.instruction: Adjust event probabilities and observe outcomes.

content.concept: Probability represents the likelihood of an event occurring and ranges from impossible to certain.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Map Population and Sample
activities.instruction: Connect each statistical concept to its role.

content.concept: A population contains the full group of interest, while a sample represents a subset used for analysis.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Sequence the Sampling Process
activities.instruction: Arrange the sampling steps in order.

content.concept: Statistical inference begins with defining a population, selecting a sample, analyzing it, and drawing conclusions with uncertainty.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Choose the Statistical Method
activities.instruction: Select the appropriate method for each scenario.

content.concept: Different analytical questions require different statistical approaches and sampling strategies.
